title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This sits in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes that follow La Longue Marche. Grothendieck is solving, in GL(2,Z_ℓ), the equation (87) g·ρ(g)·ρ²(g)=1. Here ρ is (conjugation by) an element r of order 3, namely r^{±1}=(-1 1;-1 0), which cyclically permutes x→y→z (with xyz=1) on the abelianised free group of rank 2. Since r³=1, the equation is equivalent to (g r)³=1. It is a linearised, abelianised shadow of the cyclic 'loop' relation for automorphisms of the profinite π1 of P¹−{0,1,∞}, the hexagon-type relation in GT.

Previous page. Two cases were split off. Case 1°, a+b≠0, gives c+d−b=1/δ and δ³=1. Case 2°, a+b=0, gives a=−b and d=−δ/b−c. The equation then reduces to (87a) b³=δ³=1 and (87b) c((bδ)²+bδ+1)+(δ²+b²δ+b)=0.

This page.
(a) Subcase bδ=1. Then b=δ^{-1}=δ² and (87b) becomes 3c+δ²+2δ^{-1}=3c+3δ²=0, so c=−δ²=−1/δ. Z_ℓ is torsion-free, so this holds even for ℓ=3. Hence (90): g=(−δ' δ'; −δ' 0)=δ'·(−1 1;−1 0), with δ'=1/δ=δ² and the only condition δ³=1. So g is a scalar cube root of unity times r^{∓1}, and gr is scalar. This is the exceptional case 2° of the Proposition on the next page. Here c+d−b=−2δ² ≠ 1/δ, so it is genuinely disjoint from 1°.
(b) Subcase bδ≠1. Since (bδ)³=1 in a domain, (bδ)²+bδ+1=0, and (87b) becomes (*) δ²+b²δ+b=0. Write b=uδ² with u a primitive cube root of unity. Then (*) becomes δ²(u²+u+1)=0, which holds identically. So c is free and g=(−uδ' uδ'; c, −u'δ'−c). One checks c+d−b=−δ'(u+u²)=δ', so these g fall under case 1° (a+b=0 subcase), as the Corollary on the next page states.

A longer crossed-out passage wrongly treated (*) as a further constraint (δ+u+1=0, b=δ, matrix (91)) and was abandoned. An earlier crossed-out attempt c=−(2δ²+1)/3, with a mod-3 argument, was also abandoned.

The result feeds the next page's Proposition. The solutions of gρ(g)ρ²(g)=1 are exactly those with δ³=1 and either c+d−b=1/δ, or g=δ'·r^{∓1}. In modern terms this is just the classification of g with (gr)³=1: gr is either scalar or has the appropriate trace.
errors: Case (b) silently needs a primitive cube root of unity u in Z_ℓ, i.e. ℓ≡1 mod 3. For ℓ=3 or ℓ≡2 mod 3 the subcase is empty; the page does not say so.

The step 'bδ≠1 and (bδ)³=1 ⇒ (bδ)²+bδ+1=0' uses that Z_ℓ is a domain. If the notation Ẑ_ℓ / Ẑ in the notes means the full profinite completion Ẑ=∏Z_p, this fails: one can have x³=1 with x≠1 componentwise mixed. The case split would then have to be done prime by prime.

Crossed-out errors, corrected by Grothendieck himself: the first evaluation of (87b) as 3c+(2δ²+1)=0, and the treatment of (*) as a non-trivial condition leading to δ+u+1=0 and b=δ. In fact (*) is automatic once b=uδ².
Next page (not this one): the lower-right entry is written −δu'−c. From d=−δ/b−c with b=uδ' it should be −δ'u'−c. This is either a slip or a transcription error.

ideas.what: Solving gρ(g)ρ²(g)=1 in GL2(Z_ℓ) for ρ the order-3 cyclic symmetry, equivalent to (g r)³=1. This is a linearised/abelianised version of the cyclic loop relation for Galois/GT-type automorphisms of π1(P¹−{0,1,∞}).
ideas.modern_name: abelianised (H1-level) image of the GT hexagon-type relation; elements of order dividing 3 in GL2(Z_ℓ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990), Ihara; abelianised/linear images considered by various authors
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and its 'lego'; this explicit linear computation appears unpublished

ideas.what: Case analysis on cube roots of unity: bδ=1 gives the scalar-type solution g=δ'r^{∓1}; bδ a primitive cube root gives a one-parameter family with c free.
ideas.modern_name: classification of semisimple order-3 elements / conjugacy in GL2 over Z_ℓ

missed.claim: Explicit description of the solution set of the abelianised loop equation gρ(g)ρ²(g)=1 in GL2(Z_ℓ), as a linear test case for the 'équation des lacets'. It is elementary, but it documents how Grothendieck probed the GT-type relations at the H1 level, a step that seems absent from the published record.
missed.quote: g = (−δ' δ' ; −δ' 0) où δ'=1/δ=δ², et où, je le rappelle, δ est assujetti à la seule condition δ³=1.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck testing the loop equations on their linear/abelian shadow, analogous to later studies of GT's action on abelianised fundamental groups.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine 2×2 matrix computation with cube roots of unity, partly corrected by crossing out. Mathematically elementary; only of minor historical interest as part of the linear analysis of the loop equation.
transcription_corrections: In (90) the retained matrix is (−δ' δ' ; −δ' 0), so g = δ'·(−1 1; −1 0). The next page's transcription '−δ'(−1 1; 1 0)' likely misreads signs: the matrix should have bottom row (−1 0) and carry no extra minus sign.
Line 'On aura b = u·1/δ = uδ² avec u³=1, u≠1 donc i.e. u²+u+1=0' is correct as transcribed.
The reduced equation reads 'u²+u+1=0' (Grothendieck overwrote the exponents), confirming that (*) is automatic.
The whole block from '(**) qui exige δ≠1' through (91) is struck out with diagonal lines, not just the first lines.
